summary: Provision auxiliary IAM audit-proxy role across AWS and GCP for cloud-ops debugging
description: Issue summary: Request to create a scoped, read-only ‘audit-proxy’ IAM role that SRE/cloud-ops can assume across both the AWS production org and the GCP production organization. Background: On several recent incidents we lacked a single low-privilege cross-account role that allows unified read-only access to billing, audit logs (CloudTrail/Cloud Audit Logs), and read access to house-monitoring dashboards for troubleshooting. Current ad-hoc access involves multiple service accounts and long-lived keys which increases blast radius and slows triage. Request: - Create an IAM role in AWS prod that can be assumed from the central ops AWS account (redwood-ops-prod) with the following permissions: Athena/Glue read, CloudTrail read, S3:GetObject (logs/billing buckets), CloudWatch ReadOnly, STS:AssumeRole. - Create a GCP equivalent (audit-proxy service account + IAM custom role) that allows roles/logging.viewer, bigquery.dataViewer on billing datasets, and resourcemanager.projects.get. - Bind both to a short-lived assumption policy with session duration limited to 1 hour. - Tag roles with requestor, ticket key, and expiry metadata. Business justification: Enables consistent low-privilege access pattern for on-call SREs and removes need for long-lived keys during incidents. Requestor argues this will speed median time-to-detect and median time-to-remediate for cross-cloud incidents. Requirements & constraints: - Must not grant write privileges or ability to modify IAM/policies. - Must be compatible with existing SSO/OIDC broker used for just-in-time sessions. - Must include automated expiry: roles should be rotated/invalidated automatically after 90 days unless renewed. - Any proposed policy must be reviewed by SecOps. Expiration: Temporary access tokens should be limited to 1 hour and role usage should be logged to the central audit pipeline. Approval: SecOps (Linnea Kaur) must review and sign off before production binding. Steps for SRE to validate once provisioned: 1) From redwood-ops-prod, assume AWS role via STS and list CloudTrail event history for last 24h. 2) From ops VPN, impersonate GCP audit-proxy SA and query billing dataset metadata. 3) Confirm no iam:PutRolePolicy or iam:CreatePolicy permissions are present. Links: - Existing runbook for access requests: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Cloud+Access+Runbook - Example AWS role template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/blob/main/roles/aws/audit-proxy-template.yaml - Example GCP terraform module: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/modules/gcp/iam-notes

investigation_notes: Initial audit: surveyed existing ad-hoc access patterns across prod AWS accounts and GCP org. Found three long-lived service accounts with wide read keys and two cross-account roles with excessive permisssions (one allowed iam:GetRolePolicy which is unnecessary). Logged examples and timestamps to /var/log/ops-access-audit/2026-03-09.log. Hypothesis: A templated, minimally scoped audit-proxy role will reduce need for elevated ad-hoc access and improve traceability. Tests performed: ran assume-role simulation in staging and verified CloudTrail lookup and S3 GetObject limited to /prod/logs/ prefix. Staging session duration honored 1h limit. Blocking items: AWS org SCPs may deny cross-account assume in a subset of prod child accounts; need org-policy checklist from central cloud team.
resolution: Provisioning in progress. Staging role templates validated; AWS draft PR #5027 created and updated per SecOps feedback. Pending: 1) SecOps final sign-off, 2) Org-policy exception confirmation for specific child prod accounts, 3) Terraform apply in prod with CI gating. Temporary workaround: SREs continue to use existing read-only escalation path with ticketed approval; no write access provided. Post-provision follow-ups: audit every 30 days, add role to access-review quarterly rotation.
